data.title: Diwali Muhurat trading stocks+ dividend: Expert picks 2 stocks for Samvat 2083 with record dates next week - Do you own?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- The countdown to Diwali 2026 muhurat trading session has begun, with investors gearing up to participate in the special live trading session, scheduled for November 8, Sunday. But what if your Muhurat trading stock pick also rewards with dividend opportunity?

Aurobindo Pharma and Balkrishna Industries, Mahindra & Mahindra are the three stocks recommended by Ravi Singh, Chief Research Officer from Master Capital Services Ltd. for Samvat 2083. According to the expert, these three stocks have strong potential upside over the next 12 months. Interestingly, Balkrishna Industries and Aurobindo Pharma have also fixed dividend record dates for the coming week.

The Indian stock market saw sharp reversal in trend as Nifty and Sensex staged their best ever weekly performance in years. Nifty 50 closed 2% higher after reclaiming the 25,000 levels for the first time in six months.

The Nifty 50 gained nearly 7.58% over the past week. The BSE Sensex surged 7.47% over the last five trading sessions. With the Diwali Muhurat trading session just a day away on November 8, market experts have identified three stocks that could remain in focus in Samvat 2083, with up to 25% upside potential.

The positive upside is likely to continue in the Diwali Muhurat trading session, according to Ravi Singh.

"Muhurat trading should be approached with a quality-first, long-term investment strategy rather than short-term speculation. Investors can use this auspicious session to accumulate fundamentally strong companies with healthy earnings visibility and reasonable valuations. Aurobindo Pharma, Balkrishna Industries and Mahindra & Mahindra are among the stocks worth considering, with potential upside of 13%, 14% and 25%, respectively, over the next 12 months," explained Singh.

Shares of Balkrishna Industries closed 0.18% lower at Rs.2406.90 per share. The company's board of directors had announced Rs.4 per equity share dividend. The board has fixed November 11 as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout.

Aurobindo Pharma Limited shares closed 0.49% higher at Rs.1797 per share on BSE on Friday with an Mcap of Rs.1,03,395.41 crore on Friday. The stock has delivered 57.56% return in one year. The company has announced Rs.11 per share dividend with a face value of Re 1 each. The board has fixed November 11 as the record date for the payout.

Nifty 50 and Sensex remain highly volatile during the one-hour long special Diwali Muhurat trading session and the performance is mostly driven by sentiment and relatively limited participation.

"Investors should avoid chasing sharp intraday moves, use limit orders and deploy capital gradually. The focus should remain on quality businesses and long-term wealth creation rather than treating Muhurat trading as an opportunity for aggressive short-term bets," noted the expert.

data.title: Who is Angan Guha? Ex-Wipro and Chicago Booth biz leader now CEO for Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit - Achievements
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Indian IT major Wipro on Friday announced the appointment of Angan Guha as president and chief executive officer (CEO) of its Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit. Effective 8 December 2026, he will report to Wipro CEO and Managing Director Srini Pallia and will also serve on the company's Executive Leadership Team.

The appointment marks Guha's return to Wipro, where he spent nearly three decades. According to the company's release, he will focus on building business and market momentum across the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing sectors. His responsibilities will include accelerating growth, deepening client relationships and delivering greater value to Wipro's clients in the region.

Guha will succeed Suzanne Dann, who was appointed head of the unit in October 2022. Dann left the company in May 2026, Reuters reported.

The appointment comes at a time when revenue growth in Wipro's Americas 2 Strategic Market Unit has slowed, as clients cut back on discretionary spending amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties.

As of the quarter ended 30 September 2026, Americas 2 accounted for 25.6% of Wipro's total revenue, making it the company's third-largest strategic market unit by revenue contribution.

Speaking about his appointment, Guha said, "I am honored and excited to rejoin Wipro at such a pivotal time for our industry." He added, "The evolving AI landscape presents unprecedented opportunities for businesses to innovate and lead. I look forward to collaborating with the talented team at Wipro and helping clients navigate this transformation, drive meaningful business outcomes, and build on Wipro's strong consulting and technology capabilities."

Commenting on the appointment, Pallia said, "We are delighted to welcome Angan to Wipro's leadership team," adding, "His experience in driving business growth, combined with his focus on innovation and execution, will be valuable as we strengthen our Americas business. I am confident that his leadership will help us accelerate growth, deepen client relationships, and deliver greater value to our clients."

Wipro describes Guha as an experienced technology and business leader with more than three decades of experience in driving growth, digital transformation, and client success across the BFSI, Energy & Utilities, and Manufacturing sectors.

According to his LinkedIn profile, Guha studied at G.D. Somani Memorial School before pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering in Electronics Engineering from Savitribai Phule Pune University. He also completed management programmes at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.

Before joining Wipro, Guha worked as a marketing executive at Decibels Electronics. According to a regulatory filing by Birlasoft, he joined Wipro in 1994 as an account manager and went on to hold several leadership positions during his nearly three-decade tenure.

According to Guha's profile on Wipro's website, he held leadership roles across India, the UK and the US. He went on to lead Wipro's Americas 2 business unit as its CEO and served on the company's Group Executive Council and Executive Board.

In December 2022, Guha joined Birlasoft as its CEO and managing director. He was responsible for providing strategic leadership and driving the company's growth and transformation.

data.title: The 10-Point: Trump Turns to a Hard-Line Adviser as His Political Challenges Mount — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
Emma Tucker

1. FROM MY DESK

President Trump has responded to a stunning midterm defeat by elevating one of his most combative advisers.

Stephen Miller, the architect of Trump's aggressive immigration policies, is replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles was seen as a moderating force on the president. Miller, by contrast, has long advocated a no-holds-barred approach to governing.

With Democrats taking control of Congress, Miller is expected to push for greater use of executive power and a confrontational response to congressional investigations. Our reporters explain why his appointment signals that Trump has little intention of changing course after the election.

And for a closer look at the man stepping into one of Washington's most powerful jobs, here are five things to know about Miller.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • With Wiles's departure, big business has lost a sympathetic ear in the White House.
  • Vice President JD Vance and Gulf allies are pressing Trump to end the Iran war, but other advisers are making the case for renewed attacks.
  • Elon Musk-run companies like SpaceX and Tesla have flourished in Texas thanks to white-glove treatment from elected officials. But that is about to change, Texas Democrats say.
  • A dirty tricks campaign rattled Europe this week, leaving officials convinced a barrage of bomb threats and cyberattacks are coordinated. The thing they can't figure out: Who's behind it?
  • The co-pilot in the Florida Learjet crash was 20-year-old Nathalia Filgueiras. Her dedication to flying in her teens wasn't an anomaly, but part of a growing wave of young people getting an early start in their pilot careers.
  • Jacked up by protein-heavy diet trends and a multitude of wellness fads, breakfast these days is increasingly likely to resemble its far heftier cousin: dinner.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • This week brought AI investors to the brink, as Democrats' midterm victories supercharged anxieties that had been building in the run-up to the vote. Thursday's selloff erased $2.5 trillion in market value from the Nasdaq composite, pushing it into correction territory. Hedge funds dumped positions, while systematic trades amplified the losses.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

The U.S. is emerging as the last true profit engine for the world's carmakers.

Volkswagen is considering making its first American pickup in 40 years, while Nissan is promising more rugged SUVs. Automakers around the world are focused on the U.S. because of Americans' proclivity for large vehicles and SUVs, as well as their willingness to swallow record-high sticker prices. So what happened? As Sharon Terlep reports, China's auto market faces a massive overcapacity crisis, and low-cost vehicles have conquered overseas markets and battered European automakers. Now, with rivals targeting the U.S., Detroit automakers are racing to maintain their high margins in the heartland.

5.

The midterms have given new life to an enduring American tradition.

For generations, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Ronald Reagan shaped American politics with visions that were different in detail but harmonious in principle. Both understood that a big, complicated, disputatious country requires negotiation, nuance and a willingness to live with less than what you want. This week's Democratic victories are evidence that "the battered heart of American democracy is still beating," writes Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer Jon Meacham. His essay for the Journal examines how the midterms have revived a tradition of democratic competition and what it means for the country's future.

Take a break from the news. Sign up for the WSJ. Magazine newsletter for a weekly roundup of fashion, entertainment, design, food, travel, art, architecture and more.

6. SEE THE STORY

Democrats broke the 2028 map wide open.

The wave election that gave Democrats control of Congress and a majority of governors' offices is creating another big benefit for the party: new pathways to the White House in 2028. Democratic victories in Texas, Ohio and Iowa have scrambled early thinking about how to garner the 270 Electoral College votes needed to win. The party also won governor's races in all six familiar presidential swing states. Here's a look at the expanded battleground and the new electoral math.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

  • Saturday: New Zealand is counting votes in its general election. Berkshire Hathaway reports earnings.
  • Sunday: Israel's president has said he will task a candidate with forming the country's next government following last month's election. Formula One's São Paulo Grand Prix takes place in Brazil. Nascar crowns its Cup Series champion. The NFL holds a regular-season game in Madrid, with the Cincinnati Bengals facing the Atlanta Falcons.
  • Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER

46 square miles

That is how much territory Russian forces have gained in Ukraine this year through the end of October, compared with 1,874 square miles in 2025, according to the Institute for the Study of War. For the past two months, Russian forces have lost more land than they gained as Ukraine's midrange strikes have pummeled supply routes behind the front lines with a variety of drones. We mapped out how Russia is failing on the battlefield.

9. AND FINALLY...

Here's the reading list for the hottest class at Harvard.

After our recent article about the surge in popularity of a humanities course for Harvard freshmen, readers asked us for the syllabus. And we're happy to oblige. Here's the reading list for the 2026-27 school year, along with the full list of assignments from previous years. The selections range from Homer's "The Odyssey" to James Baldwin's "The Fire Next Time." Consider this your invitation to take on a Harvard reading challenge of your own.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

  • Opinion: If Thursday's stock-market correction was a warning, Friday's modest market rebound and solid jobs report constitute a reprieve. Newly elected Democrats are inheriting a growing economy. If they can keep it.
  • WSJ | Buy Side: How many credit cards should you have? The right number depends on your financial habits, credit history, spending needs and ability to manage payments.

ABOUT US

The 10-Point is your guide to The Wall Street Journal's reporting and analysis you can't get anywhere else. Your subscription makes our journalism possible.

data.title: Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer favors Bitcoin over gold amid sell-off
data.description:
Bitcoin and gold both took a hit in the latest market sell-off. According to Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer, only one of them handled it with any grace.

Timmer, Fidelity's Director of Global Macro, says he prefers Bitcoin over gold right now. His reasoning is simple: Bitcoin's price measured against gold has held up while both assets slid.

Timmer isn't saying Bitcoin went up while gold went down. Both assets declined during the sell-off, which the research places around November 6-7.

His focus is the ratio between them. On that scoreboard, Bitcoin looks strong. One Bitcoin bought approximately 12 ounces of gold at its low point in this cycle. It now buys roughly 21 ounces.

The move has also pushed Bitcoin above the recent trading range it held against gold. For technical analysts, a break like that often signals a change in leadership between two assets.

Timmer has a habit of tracking these shifts closely. He has recorded several rotations of speculative capital between Bitcoin and gold since late 2025.

Those rotations picked up after Bitcoin peaked close to $126,000 in 2025 and gold's own momentum began to fade.

Timmer's preference lines up with where institutional money has been going. Since 2024, spot Bitcoin ETFs have pulled in nearly $55 billion in inflows.

Gold and silver exchange-traded products, by comparison, have attracted around $29 billion over the same stretch. That puts Bitcoin funds at roughly double the precious metals haul.

Both Bitcoin and gold have recently shown a correlation of 60-70% with the S&P 500. In other words, when stocks fall, these two have tended to fall alongside them.

Timmer has not abandoned gold entirely. He continues to endorse both assets as tools for diversifying against monetary and fiscal instability.

His current lean toward Bitcoin is about near-term prospects. It is a tactical tilt, not a declaration that gold has lost its place in a portfolio.

For investors, the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio is a useful lens because it strips out the noise of the dollar. It shows how two competing hedges stack up against each other directly.

The recovery from about 12 ounces to about 21 ounces suggests the pendulum has swung back toward Bitcoin, at least for now. Timmer's own record of documented rotations, however, is a reminder that this pendulum has swung several times recently.

The most immediate takeaway is that a prominent Fidelity strategist sees Bitcoin holding its ground better than gold under pressure.

The ETF flow data supports the idea that institutions are already leaning this way. A gap of nearly $55 billion versus around $29 billion is hard to dismiss as a rounding error.

Yet the high correlation with stocks is a real risk. If both assets keep tracking the S&P 500 at 60-70%, their value as diversifiers shrinks during broad market drawdowns.

Timmer's position sits somewhere in the middle. He holds both as hedges against monetary and fiscal turbulence while tilting toward the one showing better relative strength.

data.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $411.9M on Friday as BlackRock Drives the Selling
data.description:
TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net $411.9 million outflow on November 6, according to Farside Investors. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $403 million in redemptions, while Fidelity’s FBTC attracted $42.8 million. The split matters more than a simplistic claim that every institutional investor was selling.

US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds ended the week with another difficult session. Farside Investors’ November 6 fund table shows $411.9 million leaving the group on a net basis, taking November’s first five trading sessions to approximately $1.28 billion in withdrawals. That is a meaningful reversal from the calmer periods in which ETF creations helped absorb supply.

But Friday’s figures tell a more interesting story than the headline total. The redemptions were highly concentrated, and one big issuer moved in the opposite direction.

BlackRock’s fund accounts for most of the outflow

IBIT recorded a $403 million net outflow on November 6. Bitwise’s BITB lost $20.5 million, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB lost $20.1 million and Grayscale’s GBTC lost $11.1 million. Against that, Fidelity’s FBTC brought in $42.8 million. Several other funds recorded zero flows in the published table. The sum produces a large negative number, but not a uniform retreat across products.

That distinction matters because an ETF creation or redemption is activity inside a particular listed vehicle. It tells us about changes in fund shares and exposure, not the identities of the investors involved or whether they immediately sold Bitcoin on an exchange. An asset manager could rebalance between issuers; a trading desk could adjust inventory; a portfolio could change its overall risk allocation. The public flow table does not resolve those motivations.

Earlier in the week, November 4 actually brought a $74.6 million net inflow, helped by a substantial positive day for Fidelity. Our coverage of November 2’s $398.6 million outflow documented a similarly concentrated session. The developing question is whether this is a persistent reduction in aggregate exposure or particularly volatile movement through a few large products.

Why repeated redemptions matter to Bitcoin

ETFs offer one of the clearest daily public windows into demand for regulated Bitcoin exposure. Repeated net withdrawals can weaken market confidence, particularly when liquidity is already thin or leveraged traders are reducing positions. Yet the ETF market is only one part of Bitcoin’s trading ecosystem. Spot exchanges, derivatives markets, corporate treasuries and long-term holders all affect the price.

It would also be a mistake to turn the week’s flow figures into a mechanical price prediction. Timing differs between trading, share creation, custody arrangements and hedge adjustments. Fund flows can accompany an existing move as readily as they can help drive one. The visible data establish a withdrawal from ETFs; they do not establish an inevitable next price level.

The fund-level split deserves continued attention. Fidelity’s positive session shows there were still buyers of this particular wrapper even as IBIT saw substantial redemptions. If outflows broaden to more issuers and persist for several sessions, the argument for a wider risk reduction becomes stronger. If the next week reverses, Friday could look more like a volatile reallocation.

The signals worth watching next

The next useful comparisons are net creations across the largest funds, aggregate trading volume and whether redemptions occur alongside lower spot liquidity. Readers should also distinguish a final daily figure from preliminary reporting as ETF data providers update their tables.

The deeper context is why these funds became so significant. As NewsBTC previously examined when Bitcoin hashrate rebounded, the network’s underlying activity and the investment products tracking its price operate on different timescales. For now, the verified conclusion is clear: November 6 was another outflow day, and BlackRock accounted for most of the selling pressure recorded within the ETF category.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: A Cheap Play on the Aluminum Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
Alcoa may not be what it once was, but there's plenty of upside for investors.

By Andrew Bary

Alcoa offers an inexpensive play on an underappreciated commodity.

Alcoa might not be what it once was — a global industrial behemoth that was a member of the Dow Jones Industrial Average for more than 50 years, until 2013. But there is plenty of appeal for investors in a smaller Alcoa following the spinoff of its aluminum products business in 2016.

Here's why. Alcoa is the leading North American-based aluminum company. It has major operations in Australia, Brazil, and Canada, and a smaller footprint in the U.S., where it operates two of the country's four remaining aluminum smelters.

Alcoa has a presence in all stages of aluminum production. That involves the mining of bauxite, the purification of that ore into the intermediate compound of alumina, and the smelting of alumina to make aluminum using an electricity-intensive process. That method was developed by Alcoa in the late-19th century and remains little changed today.

The company's prospects are promising.

Alcoa produces about 3% of the world's aluminum, and is poised to increase its output by more than 30% to more than three million metric tons annually. That's thanks to its $4 billion purchase of AliGroup, a division of Australia's South32, which is due to close by the middle of 2027.

Alcoa's volatile shares look appealing. At around $38, they are trading just above their 52-week low, and for less than half their high of $85 in June. Alcoa trades for just six times projected 2026 earnings of $6.81 a share and seven times estimated 2027 profits of $5.50 a share.

That's low relative to mining peers, which generally fetch over 10 times earnings, and a third the S&P 500 multiple. Plus, the company produced ample free cash flow of about $600 million in the first nine months of 2026.

"Alcoa is a best-in-class integrated producer in an attractive commodity," says Steve Galbraith, managing member of Kindred Capital in Darien, Conn. He says the stock price drop since June is excessive, given that aluminum prices are down about 15% from their June high to $3,100 per metric ton, or $1.40 a pound. That means that Alcoa remains solidly profitable, given production costs of about $2,500 per ton.

"There has been no major downgrade in earnings estimates," Galbraith adds, "no crazy decline in the forward curve for aluminum prices and [global production] capacity has been relatively restrained." He believes the stock has upside of 50% from here.

In the metals space, copper has generated more excitement than aluminum because of tight market conditions, limited new supply, and electrification demand. The case for aluminum also looks good.

"There is growing demand driven by a number of megatrends like electrification and the energy transition, and strong packaging demand. Supply is constrained," Alcoa CEO William Oplinger told Barron's in an interview.

The metal's combination of strength and low weight make it ideal for aerospace, transportation, packaging, and other uses.

So, why is Alcoa trading so cheaply? Several reasons.

Investors are taking a wait-and-see approach to its AliGroup acquisition. Oplinger sees strong strategic and financial merit to the deal, which Alcoa unveiled at midyear. Integration and execution will be important. Alcoa is financing the deal mostly with debt, which will add some leverage to a balance sheet that is much improved over the past few years. Alcoa had just $1 billion of net debt before the coming transaction.

Wall Street reviews have been good so far. Jefferies analyst Chris LaFemina wrote in a recent client note that he sees "a path to a simpler and better Alcoa that we believe isn't fully reflected in the Alcoa share price."

Barclays analyst Richard Garchitorena recently initiated coverage of Alcoa with an Overweight rating and $55 price target, calling it a "crouching tiger, hidden dragon." His view: Lower aluminum prices are factored into the shares — and the AliGroup deal was smart, and is a potential 2027 catalyst due in part to $900 million in total projected synergies including logistics, technology improvements, and some cost reductions.

Another plus for investors: Alcoa's small market value of $10 billion, solid industry position, and scarcity value could make it a takeover candidate in the consolidating mining industry, although the company may have created a poison pill with the AliGroup deal.

One worry for investors: Aluminum prices spiked after the start of the Iran war, as Middle East production was curtailed. An end to the conflict could be a negative because of potentially higher output in the region, pressuring prices.

Tariffs are also an issue for Alcoa because Canadian aluminum — including sizable production from Alcoa's Quebec facilities — are subject to a 50% U.S. tariff. But for Alcoa, the tariffs are offset by high U.S. aluminum prices to the world benchmark. That is a reflection of scant domestic production relative to demand.

Aluminum demand is expected to exceed production this year, but some on Wall Street are concerned that supply could top demand in the coming years due to new production from Indonesia.

There's also the China factor. China accounts for about 60% of annual aluminum production and a similar amount of demand. China has imposed a cap on aluminum production to prevent oversupply, but its adherence to that cap is a risk, as is Chinese demand.

Nonetheless, global aluminum demand is expected to grow by 2% or so annually over the next decade, and by 3% in North America, a key Alcoa market.

CEO Oplinger says there are no pure-play Western companies with Alcoa's size in the aluminum market. "If someone wants to invest in the aluminum value chain, there's one choice: Alcoa."

Alcoa also is one of the better investments in the mining industry.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: The humanoid robot race heats up after Agility Robotics begins to trade
data.description:
Humanoid robot startup Agility Robotics began trading during the week. Shares were volatile in the first two days of action, showing an initial gain of more than 20% before settling back to closer to the $10 per share price used in the merger. Agility Robotics has the distinction of being the first U.S.-listed company focused purely on humanoid robots. It went public by merging with Churchill Capital Corp XI rather than through a traditional IPO.

The merger valued Agility’s existing equity at about $2.5B. The company brought in roughly $465M in gross capital before expenses. About $201M of that money comes from a private investment led by Foxconn . Nvidia and SoftBank Vision Fund 2 are also backers.

Agility highlighted that it expects to use the fresh funding to bring Digit 5 to market and expand manufacturing. Digit 5 is built to work safely near people without the safety barriers earlier versions needed. Deliveries are targeted for the first half of 2027, with general availability by the end of 2027. Digit is already deployed at nine customer facilities, including sites run by Amazon , Toyota , and GXO . The company plans to ramp up production at its RoboFab factory in Oregon and is building a new facility in Pittsburgh for software and AI work.

Agility Robotics expects annual losses to continue but has an order on its books worth more than $300M from one unnamed customer, covering 1K robots over three years. The contract requires Agility Robotics to hit delivery milestones and meet product specifications. Each Digit 5 robot will initially cost Agility about $150K in parts. The company expects that to drop to $75K at 1K robots a year and $30K at 10K a year.

Seeking Alpha analyst IPO Kitchen highlighted that Agility Robotics faces stiff competition from a number of competitors globally. In North America, the company's Digit 5 model will compete with Tesla's Optimus robot, Figure AI's 02 and 03 models, Boston Dynamics' Atlas robot, Apptronik's Apollo robot, 1X Technologies' NEO and EVE models, and Sanctuary AI's Phoenix robot. The list of competitors in Europe was noted to include Agile Robots, NEURA Robotics, and PAL Robotics, while in China, competition includes Unitree Robotics' H1 and G1 models, UBTECH Robotics' Walker robot, the Yuanzheng models from AgiBot/Zhiyuan Robotics, Fourier Intelligence's GR robot, and XPeng's IRON robot.

data.title: Platform and liquor stocks offer growth while gold remains non-productive, says Sunil Singhania
data.description:
Indian equities continue to offer superior wealth creation compared to non-productive assets like gold, according to Sunil Singhania, Founder of Abakkus Asset Manager. Speaking ahead of the Mahurat trading session, the market veteran highlighted platform companies, niche manufacturing, and the liquor sector as key growth areas in an increasingly efficient market where few stocks remain undiscovered.

With numerous analysts tracking the market, finding completely hidden ideas is difficult. Instead, generating returns depends on taking a differentiated view on growth prospects and temporary headwinds. Investors can find opportunities in sectors facing short-term regulatory hurdles, such as gold finance or pharmaceutical companies hit by inspection negatives. Stock reactions are driven by performance relative to expectations rather than absolute numbers. A company reporting 30% growth might see its stock fall if the market anticipated 32%, while a reported loss could trigger a rally if investors had braced for a steeper decline.

Within emerging themes, platform businesses operate on a clear winner-takes-all model. "If you are sure that this guy is the potential 80% market share, then you will make a lot of money," Singhania noted, pointing out that the runner-up typically secures the remaining 20% while others fail. Niche manufacturing is also emerging as a faster-growing segment, with unique businesses coming to the forefront.

Despite near-term challenges such as rising input costs, deficit monsoons, and state-specific regulatory hurdles like Telangana receivable bills, the liquor sector remains a strong consumption play. The industry is clocking faster growth rates than traditional staples, driven by premiumisation and widening social acceptance. While the space is heavily regulated, governments rely on it as a major revenue contributor, ensuring its continued expansion even as some stock valuations appear expensive.

Contrasting equities with precious metals, gold lacks the compounding benefits of corporate earnings. Buying 100 grams of gold yields no interest or dividends over 20 years, whereas a company with a ₹1,000 crore turnover could scale to ₹10,000 crore or even ₹30,000 crore over the same period. Gold also experiences long cycles, often delivering no returns for four to five years before a sudden spike.

Watch the full conversation here

While gold recently dropped 30% in dollar terms, domestic investors were shielded by a 10% rupee depreciation and a 10% hike in import duties, limiting the rupee-term decline to 10-15%. Silver, by comparison, has fallen 30-40%. However, the over-transparency of modern equity markets—where portfolios are tracked minute-to-minute—often hurts investor psychology compared to the less visible price movements of physical gold or real estate.

data.title: India secures place in Cup of Nations, set to compete against 18 international teams
data.description:
Mumbai, Nov. 7 -- India marked a significant milestone in its motorsport journey, earning a place in Cup of Nations, which will see 18 international teams compete for the global championship in Mumbai from November 7-9 2026, organised by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited (MFRL) in partnership with Formula 1.

Representing the country on this prestigious international platform will be Karl Verghese and Siddharth Sathgare, following Karl Verghese's crowning as the National Champion in the Open Category at the F1 Sim Racing India 2026. The development marks an important step in India's emergence on the global sim racing stage and its ambition to nurture homegrown talent capable of competing against the world's best, as per a press release.

Verghese finished with 150 points, while fellow Mumbaikar Siddharth Sathgare secured second place with 96 points and Chennai's Amith Kutti finished third with 91 points. The podium finishers maintained their distance from the rest of the pack throughout the six-race competition, with an intense contest between them. However, Karl remained unbeaten across all six races to establish his dominance in the category.

In the Under-15 category, 10-year-old Vihaan Joshi from Mumbai was crowned champion after winning five of the six races. Agastya Ivan Crasto, also from Mumbai, finished second, while Hridaan Sanadhya from Pune secured third place. The landmark occasion also witnessed the presence of Indian cricketers Shardul Thakur and Angkrish Raghuvanshi who presented prizes to the podium finishers from both categories.

With the national champions crowned, the F1 Sim Racing India Open now moves into its international phase with the Cup of Nations, taking place from 7 to 9 November. Karl Varghese and Siddharth Sathgare will represent India against a field comprising of 18 teams of the world's top sim racing divers, many of whom are part of F1 Sim Racing outfits including Ferrari, Aston Martin, Red Bull, and Alpine. The competition will follow a double-elimination format, providing Indian racers an opportunity to test themselves against established international talent.

The F1(R) Sim Racing India Open is part of MFRL's larger ambition to build a sustainable talent pipeline for Indian motorsport. Through its One in a Billion initiative, MFRL aims to make the sport more accessible, identify promising talent, and create structured opportunities for Indian racers. Fans in Mumbai can experience the Cup of Nations live at the NSCI Dome, with tickets available through District by Zomato. data.title: AI Selloff Has Investors Panicking, But Ed Yardeni Says It’s Time To Start Buying — ‘Beware Period Is Over’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Yardeni said Thursday's selloff appeared to reflect an exaggerated reaction to several concerns, including political uncertainty following the midterm elections.
  • He pointed to the unwinding of leveraged positions as another factor behind the sharp market moves.
  • The strategist also pushed back against concerns that the election results would bring the data center construction boom to a halt.

The recent selloff in artificial intelligence stocks has rattled investors, but veteran market strategist Ed Yardeni believes the panic has created an opportunity to buy rather than a reason to head for the exits.

“I think the beware period is over. And there are buying opportunities,” Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, said during an interview with CNBC on Friday, arguing that recent market turbulence has been driven partly by panic and unwinding leverage.

AI Selloff Looks Overdone, Says Yardeni

Yardeni said Thursday's selloff appeared to reflect an exaggerated reaction to several concerns, including political uncertainty following the midterm elections, rising bond yields and questions surrounding the pace of data center construction.

He pointed to the unwinding of leveraged positions as another factor behind the sharp market moves.

“I think that the selloff we had yesterday had a lot of kind of panic involved in the way things were unwinding. I think there was a lot of leverage that came undone,” Yardeni said.

The strategist also pushed back against concerns that the election results would bring the data center construction boom to a halt, arguing that investors may be mistaking a slowdown for the end of the investment cycle.

Data Center Boom Faces ‘Speed Bumps,’ Not Roadblocks

Yardeni acknowledged that the data center industry faces mounting physical, political and financial constraints, including power availability, labor shortages, construction costs and community opposition.

However, he believes these challenges are more likely to stretch out the infrastructure investment cycle than derail it. “I think it’s speed bumps. I don’t think it’s, you know, the end of the road for data centers,” Yardeni said.

He pointed to differences in state-level approaches, noting that some states and communities would continue welcoming data center investments even as others push for tighter restrictions.

Yardeni cited Texas as an example, arguing that efforts to slow construction do not necessarily mean shutting the door on new projects.

Data Center Companies May Have To Prove Their Benefits

Yardeni conceded that winning public support for data centers will become more difficult, with developers facing greater pressure to demonstrate that their projects benefit local communities.

“They’re going to have to prove that they’re going to provide their own power, that they’re not going to be careless with water usage,” he said, while adding that the economic benefits of data centers would need to outweigh their potential costs and environmental consequences.

Yardeni also pointed to financial markets imposing discipline on the rapidly expanding neocloud sector, as concerns about heavy bond issuance began to weigh on investor appetite.

Rather than signaling the end of AI infrastructure spending, he sees these developments as signs that the industry is entering a more measured phase of growth.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.17%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 0.21%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged up by 0.06%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) rose 1.32% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) gained 1.31%.

data.title: TPG investment in Kirloskar-backed Arka Fincap: What the deal entails and how funds will be used
data.description:
Kirloskar Group-backed non-banking financial company (NBFC) Arka Fincap's investment agreement with global alternative asset management firm TPG involves an initial capital infusion of ₹525 crore, with the possibility of an additional ₹275 crore subject to specified business milestones and regulatory approvals.

The investment is being made through TPG's The Rise Funds, its impact investing platform. According to Arka's November 6 statement, the capital will support the company's expansion in secured retail lending, strengthen its geographical presence and fund investments in technology and risk management capabilities.

What does the investment deal involve?

The agreement provides for an initial investment of ₹525 crore. TPG may invest another ₹275 crore through a subsequent tranche, subject to Arka achieving specified business milestones and obtaining the necessary regulatory approvals.

The company has not disclosed the proposed equity stake or valuation as part of the announcement.

Where will the funds be deployed?

Arka plans to use the growth capital to expand its secured retail lending businesses, deepen its geographical reach and strengthen its technology and risk management infrastructure.

The company currently offers pre-owned vehicle financing, secured business loans, loans against property and wholesale lending.

What is Arka Fincap's current business size?

Arka has assets under management (AUM) of around ₹8,000 crore, of which its secured retail lending portfolio accounts for more than ₹1,000 crore.

The NBFC operates across 10 states through 146 branches and has a workforce of over 2,000 employees. It continues to operate its wholesale lending platform alongside its expanding retail business.

Who are the investors and promoters?

Arka Fincap is promoted by Kirloskar Oil Engines Limited, part of the Kirloskar Group. The company is registered with the Reserve Bank of India and carries a CRISIL AA/Stable rating.

TPG is a global alternative asset management firm with investments across private equity, impact investing, credit, real estate and other strategies. The investment in Arka is being made through The Rise Funds, which focuses on growth-stage companies across sectors including financial inclusion, healthcare, education and climate.

The transaction marks TPG's investment in Arka's next phase of expansion, with a focus on secured lending to small businesses, entrepreneurs and vehicle operators.

data.title: Japan's SuMiTB makes first investment in Indian real estate fund through HDFC Capital
data.description:
Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank (SuMiTB), a Japanese financial institution, has committed capital to HDFC Capital Development of Real Estate Affordable and Mid-Income Fund (H-DREAM Fund), marking its first investment in an Indian real estate fund.

The investment, announced on November 6, has been made through HDFC Capital Advisors’ offshore feeder fund structure established under the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) framework at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City).

H-DREAM Fund, managed by HDFC Capital Advisors, has a target corpus of $500 million, with an additional greenshoe option of $500 million. The fund has secured investor commitments of more than $400 million so far, according to the companies.

The fund provides financing to residential real estate projects focused on affordable and mid-income housing. It also requires projects it finances to follow the Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies (EDGE) green building framework.

The fund has adopted the International Finance Corporation's (IFC) Environmental and Social Performance Standards and the EDGE framework to incorporate environmental and social considerations into its investments.

For SuMiTB, the investment marks its entry into India's real estate fund market. The Japanese bank said the commitment would serve as the foundation for a longer-term relationship with HDFC Capital and the broader HDFC Group.

HDFC Capital Advisors is the real estate private equity arm of the HDFC Group and a subsidiary of HDFC Bank. Its funds together represent a platform of around $5 billion, with a focus on financing affordable and mid-income housing projects.

SuMiTB, established in 1925, is Japan's largest trust bank, with $2.1 trillion in assets under custody and $1.2 trillion in assets under management, according to the company.

data.title: Gujarat Energy to foray into Compressed Bio-Gas space with ₹100 crore investment; seeks JV partners
data.description:
Gujarat Energy Ltd (GEL), India’s largest city gas distribution company by sales volume, plans to set up around 200 tonnes per day (TPD) of compressed biogas (CBG) production capacity in the initial phase, with 100 TPD proposed in Gujarat and the remaining 100 TPD outside the State, as it looks to diversify its gas sourcing portfolio and gradually reduce dependence on imported liquefied natural gas (LNG).

The Gujarat government-owned PSU has issued an expression of interest (EOI) inviting joint venture (JV) partners to set up and operate CBG plants, with the proposed initiative involving an investment of around ₹100 crore, according to the management. “We have initiated our entry into the CBG ecosystem and have issued an EOI seeking partners to set up CBG plants. This initiative will support our CBG blending requirements, leverage existing natural gas infrastructure and in the long run reduce dependence on imported LNG,” Avantika Singh, Managing Director of Gujarat Energy, told investors on Friday.

According to the EOI, the proposed initial capacity of 200 TPD will be split equally between Gujarat and locations outside the State, with 100 TPD planned in each. The company intends to develop individual plants with capacities ranging from 10 TPD to 20 TPD, depending on feedstock availability in the respective catchment areas. GEL is proposing to hold a 49 per cent stake in the joint venture companies, with selected partners holding the remaining 51 per cent. The JV companies will own and operate the CBG plants, while Gujarat Energy will support the offtake of the gas produced through its city gas distribution (CGD) network.

The company is looking to use a mix of agricultural and organic waste as feedstock, including paddy straw, press mud, Napier grass, cattle dung, poultry litter and other agricultural residues. The feedstock mix for each plant will be finalised based on its availability in the surrounding catchment area. The proposed plants will be located either within GEL’s CGD geographical areas or near the natural gas pipeline network of Gujarat Integrated Gas Ltd (GIGL), allowing the CBG produced to be injected into and marketed through the company’s distribution network or the GIGL pipeline.

The initiative is aligned with the Centre’s GOBARdhan programme and the CBG Blending Obligation (CBO) applicable to the CGD sector, which requires gas distributors to progressively incorporate compressed biogas into their natural gas supply mix. The move comes as GEL continues to strengthen its long-term LNG procurement portfolio. The company imported 24 LNG cargoes in the first half of FY27, compared with 14 in the corresponding period last year, and is targeting a sourcing portfolio of around 4 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).

Six LNG fuelling stations

The company is also exploring the development of six liquefied natural gas (LNG) fuelling stations across its geographical areas (GAs), as the city gas distributor looks to tap the potential of LNG-powered heavy commercial vehicles and expand beyond its conventional CNG and PNG distribution business.

The proposed stations are aimed at supporting the adoption of LNG in long-haul transportation, an emerging segment for gas distribution companies seeking to increase natural gas consumption in the road transport sector. “We are also exploring the development of six LNG stations in our GAs with the objective of supporting the adoption of LNG in long-haul transportation,” Singh, added.

The proposed expansion would add another segment to the company’s existing gas distribution operations, which include CNG stations for vehicles, domestic and commercial PNG connections and industrial gas supplies. LNG is being explored as an alternative fuel for heavy-duty trucks operating over long distances. Its potential in this segment stems from the possibility of using liquefied natural gas in vehicles requiring higher fuel storage capacity and longer driving ranges than conventional CNG-powered vehicles.

The company has already built a domestic PNG base of approximately 25.3 lakh connections, alongside around 17,000 commercial and 4,500 industrial connections.

data.title: Nifty may underperform broader market as half its constituents lag GDP growth: Sunil Singhania
data.description:
India's benchmark Nifty index could underperform the broader market over time, as nearly half of its constituent companies may struggle to grow in line with the country's gross domestic product (GDP), according to Sunil Singhania, Founder of Abakkus Asset Manager.

Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Singhania outlined an impending shift in market leadership as India transitions from a $4 trillion to an $8 trillion economy. He said traditional heavyweights in sectors such as fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), oil and gas, and information technology (IT) face structural limitations to growth.

"If you actually look at the composition of Nifty, 40-50% of the companies will not even grow in line with the GDP, not because something is wrong with them, but the sector is like that," Singhania said.

He added that IT services companies may find it difficult to grow beyond 2% to 3% operationally, while the currency depreciation benefit that the sector enjoyed in the past is now reversing.

With the rupee moving towards the 94 mark against the US dollar, Singhania said currency-led growth would become increasingly challenging for IT companies. Instead, he expects the next phase of growth to emerge from opportunities beyond traditional banking and generic pharmaceuticals.

Within the financial services space, Singhania sees significant potential in capital market businesses. He expects India's investor base to expand from around 13 crore currently to between 20 crore and 25 crore over time.

In healthcare, he favours hospitals, diagnostic centres and differentiated pharmaceutical companies capable of generating margins of 35% to 40%, rather than generic drugmakers operating at margins of 10% to 12%.

Singhania also pointed to the improving financial performance of several high price-to-earnings (P/E) platform companies, including Lenskart Solutions, Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww), FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa), Honasa Consumer and Shadowfax Technologies.

While acknowledging his firm's value-conscious investment approach, he said these companies were showing improving fundamentals, supported by strong growth and positive unit economics.

"The growth is good... because the unit economics is positive. The delta on the EBITA is very, very high," he said.

Why Singhania is bullish on microcaps

Beyond large- and mid-cap stocks, Singhania said Abakkus also remains active in the microcap space, which he likened to venture capital investing, but with the added advantages of liquidity and regulatory oversight.

"This is venture investment with some liquidity because they are listed. And the good thing is once you are listed, there is some compliance," Singhania said.

He cautioned that microcap investments carry risks, particularly around disclosure standards and organisational depth. However, he noted that the segment offers opportunities to invest in passionate entrepreneurs building businesses in differentiated niches and driving rapid growth.

data.title: Explained: What is the ethanol issue in Karnataka and why have OMCs rejected the state govt's excess blending claims?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- State-run oil marketing companies (OMCs) Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) have rejected Karnataka's allegations that petrol sold at some retail outlets in the state contained ethanol levels exceeding the prescribed 20% limit.

The companies questioned the sampling and testing procedures adopted by the state government, saying the reported findings could not be independently verified against the prescribed technical standards.

In a joint statement on Friday, the three OMCs said the claims that petrol sold at certain outlets contained between 26% and 31% ethanol were not supported by tests conducted in accordance with statutory and technical procedures, ANI reported. They maintained that the E20 petrol supplied by them across the country, including Karnataka, complies with the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specification IS 17021.

The companies raised concerns over the sampling exercise conducted in October 2026, alleging that samples were collected without the participation of OMC representatives. They also said they had not received the corresponding retention samples, complete outlet-wise details or laboratory reports, despite seeking these through the State Level Coordinator.

The dispute follows the Karnataka government's claim that tests of petrol samples collected from seven districts found ethanol concentrations above the E20 limit. According to a state government statement cited by Hindustan Times, 11 of 14 samples tested exceeded the 20% threshold.

The highest concentration, 31.2%, was recorded in a sample collected from an IOCL outlet. An HPCL Power sample contained 30.5% ethanol, while another HPCL sample recorded 27%. A BPCL Speed sample had an ethanol concentration of 26.5%.

The samples were collected from fuel stations in Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru. The state government said the testing was conducted at the Shriram Research Institute in Bengaluru using gas chromatography.

The oil companies said the October exercise did not follow the sampling, retention and testing procedures prescribed under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024.

Under the prescribed procedure, six one-litre samples must be collected. Two are to be handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to a laboratory specified under the Control Order or notified in the Official Gazette. The sample labels must also be jointly signed, with test results communicated to the dealer and oil company within the prescribed timeframe.

The OMCs said samples collected during Karnataka's September 2026 exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated OMC laboratories and tested for the quality parameters required under the MDG 2024. However, they alleged that the subsequent October exercise was conducted without their representatives.

The companies also questioned the laboratory certificates cited by the state government, saying they did not specify the complete technical details needed to validate the reported ethanol concentrations.

According to the OMCs, IS 17021:2018, including Amendment No. 3 issued in August 2025, prescribes methods for determining ethanol content in E20 fuel. These include Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) under ASTM D5845, water extraction under Annex C, or Gas Chromatography under ASTM D4815/D6839.

The companies said that when gas chromatography is used, the sample must first be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol, and the result corrected against an E10 certified reference material. They argued that the certificates cited by Karnataka merely mentioned ethanol percentage by gas chromatography without specifying the applicable standard, dilution procedure or reference material.

In the absence of these details and counterpart samples, the OMCs said, the reported ethanol levels of 26-31% could not be independently validated against the prescribed methodology.

The three companies also cited a joint quality-monitoring exercise conducted with the Centre for High Technology. They said all 893 E20 samples tested from their depots and retail outlets across 27 states and Union territories were within the prescribed ethanol range of 19-21%.

The exercise included 56 samples from Karnataka, which recorded ethanol concentrations between 19% and 20%, with an average of 19.30%, according to the OMCs.

They said ethanol blending at their refineries and depots is carried out through calibrated and controlled systems, with automatic calibration and proportioning arrangements governing the process.

The companies also argued that more than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years. They said there had been no widespread reports of vehicle breakdowns that would indicate a systemic fuel-quality problem.

The Karnataka government has raised concerns about the impact of higher ethanol concentrations on vehicle performance and fuel efficiency, particularly in vehicles designed to operate with lower ethanol blends.

The state estimated that motorists could be losing around Rs.62,000 crore annually due to lower mileage, assuming a 10% reduction in fuel efficiency across the vehicle population. It separately estimated annual vehicle-repair costs at Rs.39,000 crore, taking the combined potential burden to approximately Rs.1.01 lakh crore.

The OMCs rejected these estimates, saying that applying a blanket assumption of 10% mileage loss across the entire vehicle population does not constitute a scientifically established assessment. They also said the repair-cost estimate needed to be supported by actual vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs.

Karnataka has sought an explanation from the Union government on the ethanol concentrations found in the samples and called for action against oil companies found selling petrol containing more than 20% ethanol. The state has also demanded that petrol stations disclose the ethanol content of the fuel they sell and allow consumers to choose between available blends.

data.title: ONGC Videsh's eyes on two Venezuela oil projects; know what finance head Anupam Agarwal said on $500 mn dividend
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- The Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) finance head, Anupam Agarwal, reportedly said on Friday that ONGC Videsh's (OVL) pending $500 million in dividends from two projects in Venezuela are likely to be adjusted once new operator agreements are finalised.

ONGC Videsh, the overseas investment arm of ONGC, has over $500 million in pending dividend from its stakes in the two projects: San Cristobal and Carabobo 1 field.

India's top explorer ONGC hopes to secure rights to operate two Venezuelan oil projects within three to six months, as it is in advanced talks with Venezuelan and US authorities, its head of finance, Anupam Agarwal, said on Friday during an analyst call.

According to the report, ONGC Videsh is exploring the possibility of securing operatorship rights for two Venezuelan oil projects - San Cristobal and PetroCarabobo - and is in advanced talks with the Venezuelan govt and US authorities.

During an analyst call following its Q2 financial results, the company reportedly said the arrangement is likely to be finalised in three to six months.

"The pending dividend from the two projects will be adjusted after the new operatorship agreements are finalised," Agarwal was quoted by PTI as saying.

The proposed agreements would give OVL - previously only an investor - greater control over field operations, production, marketing and handling of revenues. Under the new arrangement, the Indian company would operate the projects and sell its output.

The new arrangement also includes a clause that could allow ONGC to take stakes in more Venezuelan fields, Agarwal said.

Agarwal said ONGC is expected to get full operatorship of the San Cristobal project, in which it holds 40 percent and Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA holds the rest, while for PetroCarabobo it would be a joint operatorship with other investors.

In the Carabobo project, ONGC and other Indian companies hold an 18 percent stake while Spain's Repsol has 11 percent, PTI reported.

Agarwal also said production from Russia's Sakhalin-1 project, in which ONGC holds 20 percent, averaged about 183,000 barrels per day in April-September, similar to the level recorded before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
